title: Bad-event probability under junta projection
statement: Let $n,M,R$ be nonnegative integers, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a sign-valued Boolean function, let $P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a set of coordinates, and fix a sign assignment $z$ on $P$. Let $B$ be a property of batches of $M$ pairs, each consisting of an assignment to the coordinates outside $P$ and a sign. If a uniformly random batch of $M$ independent uniform assignments to those outside coordinates, labeled by the restriction of $f$ with the fixed coordinates set to $z$, satisfies $B$ with probability at most $\eta$, then for $R$ independent uniform inputs in $\{-1,1\}^n$, the probability that the procedure selecting up to $M$ samples whose fixed coordinates match $z$ returns a batch satisfying $B$ is at most $\eta$; failure to return a batch is not counted as a bad outcome.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued Boolean function on $n$ bits
$P$ is a finite set of coordinates among the $n$ bits
$B$ is a property of batches of $M$ free-coordinate assignments with sign labels
The ideal labeled-batch probability under the uniform distribution is at most $\eta$
